about: The Rock Eyebrow Raise is a selfie-style close-up of Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson leaning toward the camera, one eyebrow cocked high, eyes narrowed and mouth pressed into a skeptical line. He is looking at you as if you just said something deeply suspicious. The meme uses that look as a reaction to anything sus: a weird excuse, an oddly specific claim, a statement that sounds innocent but clearly isn't. It inherits his wrestling-era trademark, the "People's Eyebrow", which was always about calling someone's nonsense without saying a word.
origin: Johnson made the raised eyebrow a signature move during his WWE career. Clips of him raising it in a video selfie, often paired with a loud bass thud, became a popular suspicion reaction around 2021.
usage:
Split the suspicious statement across the two boxes: top box starts the quote, bottom box finishes it so the reader hits the questionable part right when they reach the eyebrow again. Phrasing it as something someone said to you ("you said the feature" / "was 'basically done'?") works well.

It lands best on excuses and claims that are technically possible but highly unlikely: a teammate's "my controller disconnected", a kid saying the dog ate the homework, a store's "limited time" sale that never ends. Keep the tone accusatory but playful.
ideas: for the third year in a row
